While it correctly identifies that stream velocity decreasing reduces the stream's capacity to carry sediment, it incorrectly concludes that erosion of the stream bank will likely increase. In standard hydrological contexts, when stream velocity decreases, the primary and most direct consequence is the deposition of sediment (Option B) because the water no longer has enough energy to transport its load. The Planner's justification relies on specific, less common conditions (like bank saturation on the falling limb of a hydrograph) to override the fundamental rule that lower velocity leads to deposition, not increased erosion. This leads to the wrong final answer (A) instead of the correct answer (B).
